- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.25) or erratic, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ in 3-day window); apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use 7-day moving average as smoothing filter before forecasting.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +0.5 and -0.3), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast to sentiment median rather than peak.
